description.narrative: Malawi¿s economy and livelihoods are overwhelmingly dependent on agriculture, which employs the majority of the population but suffers from low productivity, fragmented markets, and growing vulnerability to climate shocks. Despite strong national policy commitments and framework, food insecurity affects almost a third of the population. Yet, rice, soybeans and coffee stand out as priority value chains with high growth potential, supported by dedicated national strategies and regional frameworks. These crops combine opportunities for import substitution and export growth with inclusivity for smallholders and women, and synergies with ongoing EU interventions and Team Europe Initiatives (TEIs). AgriCatalyst Malawi directly contributes to the NDICI MIP 2021¿2027 Priority 1 ¿ Green and Resilient Economic Transformation and the EU Global Gateway. It will help Malawi move from subsistence agriculture to competitive and climate-resilient agri-food systems, while advancing the EU Green Deal and the Gender Action Plan III.The Overall Objective is todevelop more competitive, inclusive, sustainable and climate-resilient rice, soybeans and coffee value chains contributing to sustainable agri-food systems transformation. The Specific Objectives are (1) Enhanced productivity and commercialization of commercially viable agribusiness groups in priority value chains; (2) Improved climate resilience and sustainable resource management capacities of commercially viable agribusiness groups in priority value chains.AgriCatalyst rests therefore on two complementary components. The first focuses on productivity and commercialisation, recognising that smallholder farmers and agribusinesses cannot grow without access to adequate infrastructure, finance, and organisational capacity. Investments in last-mile facilities, blended rural finance, and entrepreneurial skills will enable farmers¿ organisations and SMEs to reach markets, attract buyers, and capture more value. The second component addresses climate resilience and sustainable resource management, acknowledging that productivity gains will not last unless natural capital is safeguarded. By strengthening seed systems, diversifying farming practices, and scaling agroecology, the Action will help farmers adapt to climate change, restore soil fertility, and reduce environmental degradation. These measures also respond to systemic challenges such as declining seed quality, soil erosion, and over-reliance on rain-fed systems. Together, the two components create a balanced approach: infrastructure and finance make commercialisation possible, while resilient farming systems ensure that growth is sustainable and inclusive. AgriCatalyst contributes to SDGs 1, 2, 5, 8, 9 and 13, with significant markers for gender, environment, climate change, digitalization, and reduction of inequalities. It is embedded in the TEI Green Growth for Malawi and promotes the links with continental TEI on coffee. It will leverage blended finance through the Malawi Agricultural & Industrial Investment Corporation (MAIIC). Overall, it seeks transformative impact: more competitive and sustainable value chains, higher incomes, improved food security, and reduced gender inequalities.
